cards.b: Biotic: living parts of an ecosystem (plants, animals). Abiotic: non-living parts (temperature, salinity, light, soil).
Warm (about 23–29°C), clear, shallow, sunlit, salty water in tropical seas between about 30°N and 30°S.
Very high biodiversity, protect coasts by absorbing wave energy, and support tourism and fishing.
Salt-tolerant trees in muddy tropical shores with stilt roots. Nursery for fish, trap sediment, slow waves.
Muddy, salty, tidal land in sheltered estuaries, with salt-tolerant plants. Absorbs wave energy and supports birds.
Windblown sand stabilised by marram grass, which has long roots. Dunes act as a natural sea defence.
Stressed corals (warm water, pollution) expel their algae and turn white. Many then die.
Anchors and divers damage reefs; sewage and waste pollute water; hotels built on dunes and mangroves.
Fertiliser and soil runoff cause algal blooms and cloudy water; pesticides poison marine life.
A rise in sea level caused by low air pressure and strong winds, especially at high tide.
Storm surges, tsunamis and climate change (sea-level rise and stronger storms).
Very effective at stopping erosion and flooding. But very expensive, can be ugly and erode at the base.
Trap sediment and build beaches, relatively cheap. But starve beaches downdrift, causing more erosion there.
Rip-rap: large boulders piled at the cliff base. Gabions: wire cages of stones. Cheap but can look unattractive.
Adding sand or shingle to the beach. Natural-looking and good for tourism, but must be repeated, costly and dredging harms habitats.
Allowing the sea to flood land in a planned way. Cheap and creates marsh habitat, but people lose homes and land.
Hold the line, advance the line, managed realignment (retreat), and do nothing.
Conservation protects nature but limits building; development brings jobs and income but can damage the environment.

gaps.s: Corals expel their algae and turn white in a process called coral ___.
Trees such as mangroves that live in salty tidal mud have ___ roots.
A rise in sea level caused by low pressure and strong winds is a storm ___.
Barriers built at right angles to the beach to trap sediment are called ___.
Adding sand to a beach is known as beach ___.
Planned flooding of land and moving people back is called managed ___.
Water temperature and salinity are examples of ___ factors in an ecosystem.
Plants that tolerate salt, found on salt marshes, are called ___.

short.q: Explain why mangroves are important for coastal protection.
short.model: Their roots slow waves and absorb wave energy, and trap sediment, which reduces erosion and flooding behind them.
points: roots absorb wave energy / slow water
trap sediment, reducing erosion and flooding

short.q: Give two ways that climate change threatens coral reefs.
short.model: Warmer seas cause coral bleaching, and ocean acidification weakens coral skeletons. Sea-level rise can also change light levels.

short.q: Describe one disadvantage of hard engineering on the coast.
short.model: Hard engineering such as sea walls is very expensive to build and maintain, and can increase erosion elsewhere along the coast.
points: can increase erosion elsewhere / ugly / disrupts sediment

short.q: Explain why managed retreat may be chosen instead of building a sea wall.
short.model: It is much cheaper than defending low-value land, and the flooded land can become salt marsh that absorbs wave energy and provides habitat.

short.q: State one conflict between conservationists and developers on a coast.
short.model: Developers want to build hotels or ports for jobs and income, while conservationists want to protect habitats like dunes or mangroves from damage.
